SMTO-HTTP-0032 — SMTO's web request didn't get a usable answer

GUID: cbf66fbd-562d-453f-abe2-58a708c6e281
Slug: http-transport-error
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The connection broke or the answer couldn't be read, and SMTO couldn't tell exactly why. The request may already have reached the service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task was changing something, such as creating, updating or deleting a record, look on that service to see whether the change already happened. The connection broke after sending, so the change may have gone through even though no answer came back.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway the task uses, and select Check connection. A Gateway that loses its link to SMTO in the middle of a request causes this error.
  3. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, and select Test connection. This shows whether the service itself can be reached right now.
  4. Only if the change didn't happen, or the task only read information, run the task again. Repeating a change that already went through could make it happen twice.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Reachable, and a repeated request returns a normal answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the service, saying whether the change already appeared. Don't assume the request failed just because no answer came back.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HTTP dispatch or response handling failed without a more specific classification, or the Gateway result lacked a status code and error kind; whether the target processed the request is unknown.

What this means

  • Dispatch/response processing failed without a more specific supported classification, or the Gateway result lacked a status and specific error kind. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Dispatch/response processing failed without a more specific supported classification, or the Gateway result lacked a status and specific error kind.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect recorded dispatch phase, nested typed failure and original effect state; preserve unknown mutations for reconciliation.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway log and network path for the failing request, and inspect the target's current state before repeating any write; reads can be reissued once the route is healthy. A lost Gateway response is not proof that the target did not process the request.
  • Inspect network and destination service diagnostics; establish current remote state before repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The underlying route/protocol issue is identified and any previous effect is settled before new work.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
